A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same power augmented Lagrangian work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching renumbered results and relocated experiments.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original clustering experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, random quadratic programs, generalized eigenvalue problems, and basis pursuit.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original clustering and quadratic-program experiments; Appendix B retains the generalized eigenvalue experiments.

M1.justification: The formulation expands from minimizing smooth f over a convex set X to minimizing f+g with a general convex, potentially nonsmooth g. Algorithm 1 consequently uses composite subproblems and a subdifferential-based stopping condition. The multiplier and penalty updates remain essentially unchanged; Appendix C documents previously used inner methods rather than introducing new ones.

E1.justification: The entire basis-pursuit sparse-recovery task in v1 Section 4.4 disappears, narrowing the empirical task coverage. MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, quadratic programs, and generalized eigenvalue problems remain; the eigenvalue experiment moves to Appendix B rather than being removed.

E2.justification: The retained experiments still compare power choices against nu=1, identified as classical iALM from Sahin et al. (2019), and retain the double-loop versus iPPM comparison. The inner-solver replacement changes experimental settings, while the new assumptions-comparison table introduces no empirically evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Clustering and standard QP experiments replace APGM with UPFAG and report inner iterations instead of gradient calls. Clustering changes its tolerance from 10^-5 to 10^-4 and inner cap from 5,000 to 1,500. QPs change the initial penalty from 0.01 to 5 and cap from 100,000 to 10,000, alongside other retuning. The n=400, m=80 QP setting is removed.

E4.justification: Power-sensitivity analyses are revised under the new solver, including extending the MNIST sweep to nu=0.65. The explicit larger-QP check of whether the advantage of unconventional powers persists with increased problem size is removed with v1 Table 3. The existing double-loop versus triple-loop analysis remains.

E5.justification: Both versions use individual random-instance results, trial averages, and violin distributions over 100 QPs. Neither introduces seed-based replication information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed values and removed experimental configurations do not establish a change in statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Clustering Figures 1–2 and standard-QP results are replaced under revised settings; MNIST's best plotted power shifts from 0.8 to 0.7. For nu=0.8, v1 Table 1 reports 44,494.2 average APGM gradient calls, whereas v2 Table 2 reports 61,940.3 UPFAG iterations, which are different metrics. Basis-pursuit and larger-QP results disappear. The iPPM QP table and eigenvalue Table 4 retain identical numerical entries.

T1.justification: V2 generalizes stationarity to the subdifferential of g, replaces the compact-domain assumptions in Section 2 with local smoothness and level-coercivity assumptions, revises regularity, and adds boundedness/sublevel-set Lemmas 2 and 6 with new proofs. The principal complexity exponents remain largely unchanged. The newly added nested-sublevel argument in Appendix A.1 contains a substantive gap.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion add prominent claims of handling a generic convex objective term and obtaining complexity guarantees without assuming bounded iterates. These materially broaden v1's contribution scope. The existing claims about sharper penalties, the primal–dual complexity tradeoff, and improved proximal-point complexity remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the applicability discussion: it distinguishes domain-normal-cone regularity from subdifferential formulations, discusses convex-term boundary difficulties, and acknowledges failure of spherical-constraint regularity at the origin. It also connects sharper penalties to exact penalties, explains separate tolerances through rescaling, and discusses why increasing inner budgets can be counterproductive for smaller powers.

D1.justification: V2 adds a paper-specific source-code link, whereas v1 only links an underlying APGM library. New Appendix C supplies detailed UPFAG and FGM pseudocode, projection formulas, and per-iteration operation information previously left largely to citations. Experimental hyperparameter documentation is also revised; the stated Julia environment and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The positioning expands substantially through the new assumptions-comparison Table 1 and distinctions between earlier regularity conditions and the proposed composite framework. V2 adds El Bourkhissi et al. (2025), Hermans et al. (2022), and Rockafellar (1970, 1993), while removing references associated with deleted material. The Latafat preprint-to-publication update is bibliographic rather than a new work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain recognizable. V2 revises the abstract and contribution list, adds descriptive background paragraph headings, expands explanatory passages, moves the eigenvalue section to Appendix B, and adds Appendix C and acknowledgments. These are targeted narrative and organizational revisions accompanying the substantive changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a journal layout and substantially revises the displays: Figures 1–3 have updated plots and cost-axis labels, a new assumptions table and two inner-solver algorithm boxes appear, and v1 Figure 5 and larger-QP Table 3 disappear. Eigenvalue Figure 4 and Table 4 move to Appendix B. Table styling and captions are also reformatted throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through solver pseudocode, code-access information, and experiments using the analyzed UPFAG solver. However, its central claim of dispensing with assumed boundedness relies on new Lemmas 2 and 6. In Appendix A.1, Lemma 6 substitutes an arbitrary x into a multiplier update defined at x^{k+1}, then asserts nested sublevel sets; this does not establish the claimed containment. Thus the major theoretical expansion cannot be credited as demonstrated. Together with reduced empirical coverage, this leaves substantial benefits and harms without a reliable net quality judgment.
